response.report:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, one view, 2026-11-21
CLINICAL INDICATION: Emergency department. Shortness of breath. History of prostate cancer on hormone therapy. Portable film.
ORDERING PROVIDER: Dr. J. Marte (synthetic), ED
COMPARISON: Chest radiograph, 2026-06-30. Note: the prior report reads "Heart size normal. Lungs clear" and mentions no cardiac device. The prior image shows an enlarged cardiac silhouette and a left chest wall cardiac device with transvenous leads. Please confirm the prior report belongs to this prior image.
TECHNIQUE: Current is AP, portable, labeled supine, with low lung volumes. Prior is PA and appears upright. Projection, position and inspiration all differ from the prior, so comparison is limited.

LOOK AT FIRST:
- F1/F2: Increased bilateral hazy and reticular opacity in the perihilar and mid zones (right and left) compared with the prior. Both reads agreed.
- F9: Linear densities over the tracheal air column, right upper mediastinum and upper abdomen that could be an endotracheal tube and an enteric tube or central line, or external tubing. Not present on the prior. The two reads disagreed (one indeterminate, one new), so this is indeterminate. Presence and tip positions are not confirmed.
- F3: Right basal opacity, indeterminate.
- F7: Enlarged cardiac silhouette. Change is not determinable across AP supine versus PA.

FINDINGS (systematic read, done blind to the indication):
- Airway / lungs: Trachea is roughly midline allowing for rotation. Lung volumes are low. Diffuse bilateral hazy and reticular opacity, most marked in the perihilar and mid zones, with denser opacity at both bases. Right mid zone (F1) and left mid zone (F2) opacity is increased from the prior, which showed only mildly prominent markings on the right and a largely clear left mid zone. This may reflect interstitial or alveolar fluid; other diffuse processes are not excluded. Supine position and lower volumes contribute to some of the difference. Right basal opacity partly obscuring the right hemidiaphragm (F3) is indeterminate and not comparable. Both reads called it indeterminate. Retrocardiac and left basal opacity obscuring the left hemidiaphragm (F4) is indeterminate and not comparable. Both reads called it indeterminate. No pleural line is seen, but pneumothorax cannot be excluded on a supine film.
- Mediastinum / hila: Upper mediastinum looks wide on this AP supine film and is not comparable with the prior PA. Both hila are indistinct with surrounding hazy opacity.
- Pleura: Hazy right costophrenic angle (F5) and hazy left costophrenic angle (F6). Layering pleural effusion is possible on each side. Both are indeterminate and not comparable, because the current film is supine and the prior is upright.
- Heart: Cardiac silhouette is enlarged on both studies (F7). It looks larger on the current film, but the current is AP supine with low volumes, which magnify the heart. Change is indeterminate and not comparable. Heart borders are partly blurred by adjacent lung opacity.
- Bones / soft tissue: Mottled, heterogeneous density projects over the right glenoid and scapular neck region on the current film (F10). It could be projectional from arm position and the overlying ECG electrode, or altered bone texture. It is indeterminate and not comparable. No definite sclerotic or destructive lesion is identified in the visible ribs, clavicles or spine at this resolution. No displaced rib fracture. No soft tissue gas. Review on source images in PACS is needed. Devices: left chest wall cardiac device generator with transvenous leads (F8). One lead has a coil over the right mediastinum, one coiled lead projects over the lower heart, and electrode markers project over the left heart. The configuration is similar to the prior allowing for projection. No visible lead discontinuity at this resolution. Linear densities of uncertain nature are described under F9 above. External monitoring leads are present.

INTERVAL CHANGE:
- Changed: Increased bilateral hazy and reticular perihilar and mid zone opacity (F1, F2). Linear densities over the trachea, right upper mediastinum and upper abdomen are not seen on the prior (F9). The two reads disagreed on whether they are new, so this is indeterminate. Basal opacities (F3, F4), pleural haze (F5, F6) and the right scapular density (F10) are indeterminate and not comparable. No size change is reported for the heart.
- Unchanged: Cardiac device generator and lead configuration are similar to the prior allowing for projection (F8).

RECIST 1.1: Not computed on radiographs.

CAN'T DETERMINE:
- Has the heart size changed? | Reason: Prior is PA and current is AP supine with low volumes. AP projection and low inspiration magnify the heart shadow. | Recommend: Repeat PA and lateral when the patient is able. Echocardiography if clinically relevant.
- Is the upper mediastinum widened? | Reason: The current film is AP supine with mild rotation, which widens the mediastinal shadow. Device leads cross the region. | Recommend: Repeat upright PA film when the patient is able, or CT chest if there is clinical concern.
- Are pleural effusions present, and have they changed? | Reason: The current film is supine, so fluid layers posteriorly and shows only as haze. The prior is upright. The amounts are not comparable. | Recommend: Upright or decubitus film, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest.
- Do the basal opacities reflect consolidation, collapse, layering fluid or low volumes? | Reason: Low inspiration and supine position crowd the lower zones and mimic basal opacity. The magnified heart hides the left base. | Recommend: Repeat film with good inspiration when the patient is able, or CT chest.
- Is there a pneumothorax? | Reason: No pleural line is seen, but on a supine film air collects anteriorly and at the bases and may not show. A skin fold or linen line and external wires cross the chest. | Recommend: Upright or decubitus film, or CT chest if there is clinical concern.
- Are an endotracheal tube, enteric tube or central line present, and where are the tips? | Reason: Linear densities over the trachea, right upper mediastinum and upper abdomen overlap device leads, external wires and the spine. The image is low resolution. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS with edge enhancement and correlate with the bedside record of lines and tubes. Confirm tip positions before use.
- Are there small lung nodules, or lesions behind the heart or generator? | Reason: Diffuse opacity on the current film, the device generator over the left upper chest and the enlarged heart all hide lung. The AP portable film is lower quality than the PA prior. | Recommend: CT chest if clinically relevant, or repeat PA and lateral after the diffuse opacity clears.
- Is there free gas under the diaphragm? | Reason: The current film is supine. Free gas does not collect under the diaphragm in this position. | Recommend: Upright or decubitus film if there is clinical concern.
- Is there a pleural effusion on either side, and has it changed? | Reason: The current film is supine, so fluid layers posteriorly and shows only as hazy density. Both costophrenic angles are indistinct on the current film and were clear on the upright PA prior. | Recommend: Upright or semi-erect film or decubitus views when the patient is able, or bedside ultrasound or CT chest.
- Is the upper mediastinum truly widened? | Reason: Supine AP projection with mild rotation widens the mediastinal shadow. The prior PA showed no widening. | Recommend: Repeat upright PA film when the patient is able, or CT chest if there is clinical concern.
- Is the right basal opacity consolidation, atelectasis or layering fluid? | Reason: Low lung volumes and supine position crowd the base and obscure the hemidiaphragm. A frontal film alone cannot separate these. | Recommend: Repeat film with better inspiration, upright if possible, or CT chest.
- Where exactly is the endotracheal tube tip relative to the carina, and is there an enteric tube with its tip in the stomach? | Reason: The image is low resolution and the carina is not clearly defined. A tubular density over the upper abdomen could be an enteric tube or external tubing. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS with windowing. Repeat the film if the tube positions remain unclear.
- Are there small nodules or subtle bone lesions on either study? | Reason: The device generator overlies the left upper and mid zones on both films. Diffuse opacity and portable technique on the current film hide fine detail. | Recommend: CT chest if clinically indicated. Review source images in PACS.

IMPRESSION:
1. Increased bilateral hazy and reticular perihilar and mid zone opacity compared with the prior, with bibasal opacity. This may reflect interstitial or alveolar fluid; other diffuse processes are not excluded. Supine position and low volumes contribute to some of the difference.
2. Possible endotracheal tube and enteric tube or central line, or external tubing (F9). The reads disagreed, so this is indeterminate. Presence and tip positions are not confirmed. Correlate with the bedside record and review source images in PACS.
3. Right basal opacity (F3) and left retrocardiac and basal opacity (F4) are indeterminate. Consolidation, collapse, layering fluid and low volumes cannot be separated on this film.
4. Enlarged cardiac silhouette on both studies. Change is not determinable across AP supine versus PA.
5. Pleural effusions, pneumothorax and mediastinal width are undetermined on this supine AP film. A mottled density over the right scapula (F10) is indeterminate, in a patient with prostate cancer, and needs source image review. Cardiac device is similar to the prior allowing for projection.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
- Repeat PA and lateral chest radiograph, upright, with good inspiration, when the patient is able.
- Upright or decubitus chest film if pleural effusion, pneumothorax or free gas is a clinical concern.
- CT chest if clinical concern persists for effusion, basal opacity, mediastinal widening or nodules.
- Review source images in PACS for tube and line tips, lead integrity and the right scapular density. Correlate with the bedside record of lines and tubes.
- Echocardiography if clinically relevant for heart size.

AI DRAFT: requires resident review and attending signature.
